name: compare_three_way
description: Compares an open project against a new delivery and, optionally, against the delivery both came from - the three sides of an update on support. Reports node counts, how many differ, how many exist on one side only, the metadata objects that moved by name, and the problems the environment raises. With an ancestor every changed object carries changedBy - OURS, VENDOR or BOTH - so a customisation is told apart from a vendor change and BOTH marks the conflicts; without an ancestor changedBy is UNKNOWN rather than guessed. Each object also reports the merge rule the environment itself proposes. A MERGE also takes the vendor support settings from the delivery - that cannot be prevented through the environment's merge rules, so instead the support modes are counted before and after and reported as supportModesBefore, supportModesAfter and supportModesChanged. Decisions about individual objects can be recorded and written to a settings file that EDT reads back when a person runs the merge, and a file written earlier can be read back in through decisionsFrom. Reading is the default and changes nothing. Passing A configuration with no customisations updates in one call with intent=UPDATE_UNCHANGED, which needs no decisions and refuses itself the moment anything was changed here or on both sides. intent=MERGE applies the decisions to the project, which is IRREVERSIBLE and is refused when the environment raises a blocking problem or when no decisions were given; after a merge the touched objects are revalidated and the errors standing against them are reported. Before a changing intent a restore point of the project files is taken; if it cannot be taken the merge does not start. git restore_merge_point puts those files back and does not roll back the infobase.

projectName.description: Open project that plays our side (MAIN). Required for every call except help.

otherPath.description: Directory holding the configuration to compare against (OTHER). Required for every call except help.

parentId.description: Which vendor configuration of the project the deliveries are measured against, by id or by name. Required when the project descends from more than one.

ancestorPath.description: Directory holding the common ancestor (COMMON_ANCESTOR). Omit for a two-sided comparison.

decisions.description: What to do with objects, as a JSON array: {"object":...,"rule":...} or {"select":"matching","rule":...}. Rules: GET_FROM_OTHER, DO_NOT_MERGE, MERGE_PRIORITIZING_MAIN, MERGE_PRIORITIZING_OTHER, MERGE_USING_EXTERNAL_TOOL. CUSTOM_MERGE is refused - it composes the result in the merge editor. The rule each object ends up carrying is read back from the comparison.

decisionsPath.description: Absolute path to write the recorded decisions to, in the format EDT reads back when a person runs the merge. Must end in .zip. Without it the decisions die with the comparison.

decisionsFrom.description: Absolute path to a settings file (.zip) written earlier, whose decisions and object correspondences are applied before anything else.

changedBy.description: List only objects with this attribution: OURS, VENDOR, BOTH or UNKNOWN. The counts always cover everything; OURS is what a customisation-preserving update needs to enumerate.

type.description: List only objects of this metadata type, as the comparison qualifies names (Catalog, Document, CommonModule).

oneSided.description: true lists only objects present on one side, false only those on both. Omit for either.

mustBeMergedOnly.description: List only objects the environment says must take part in a merge.

offset.description: How many matching objects to skip. Default 0.

limit.description: How many objects to name. Default and maximum 500.

sectionsOffset.description: Module pieces to skip before the page of sections starts. Default 0.

scope.description: Compare only these objects, comma separated and named as this tool names them (Catalog.X,Document.Y). Omit for the whole configuration. What the environment added comes back in scopeExtendedBy, unrecognised names in scopeUnrecognised rather than dropped.

report.description: Assemble the answer into one document a person can read before deciding to update: summary (ten names per section) or full.

methodLevel.description: Look inside modules, so a change is named CommonModule.X.Module.MethodName and a decision can be addressed at one method. Off by default; comparedInMs comes back either way, so the cost is measurable.

closeSession.description: Close the comparison after answering rather than keep it open for paging. Off by default; it expires after 20 idle minutes.

ignoreOriginMismatch.description: Compare the sides even when they do not identify as the same configuration in different versions. Off by default.

help.description: Pass a word - help=parameters - to be told what the parameters mean and nothing else; the rest of the call is then ignored. An empty or whitespace-only value is not a request, so a client that fills every declared string still compares.

intent.description: What the run does. REPORT (default) changes nothing in the project. MERGE and MERGE_IGNORING_PROBLEMS apply the decisions - IRREVERSIBLE. UPDATE_UNCHANGED takes the delivery whole. UPDATE_KEEPING_OURS is the ordinary update on support: objects both sides changed are merged with the delivery in front, methods only this side has stay, an object that will not take that merge is named in deliveryNotApplied, and it refuses outright when an object of ours could not be held at all. This applies only with methodLevel=true; WITHOUT it the comparison stops at the object and such an object is held instead. Putting the delivery in front does NOT guarantee that work only this side had survives - what came out identical to the delivery is named in ourContentLost. Why each mode behaves so, and when it refuses: help=parameters. A restore point of the project files is taken before a changing intent; without it the merge does not start. git restore_merge_point puts the files back and does not roll back the infobase.
